## Current direction — October 14, 2026

> for 566, we should be able to use `jelos`/`jelos` for now and then, create an issue to see if we can swap for different credentials.

Use the already documented shared JELOS developer identity as the interim choice (D-WORKFLOW-166). #586 tracks evaluating replacement credentials later and is not an M7 candidate prerequisite. This settles identity selection; #566 still owns provisioning so ordinary players do not enter developer credentials, with separate personal account login and source/UI/backup/clean/upgrade qualification. Current recipe behavior is unchanged in this record-only update. No new provider permission or successful authentication is inferred.

## Owner feedback — 2026-10-12

> We likely need to get our own developer username and password for screenscraper, or we should just embed, for the time being, the current password into releases instead of showing it in the developer options. I think that ROCKNIX is also using the jelos password that we're currently using, so we might be fine just using that in screenscraper.

Already written: #64 and D-QA-005/006 deliberately use device-entered developer credentials. The recipe enables SCREENSCRAPER_RUNTIME_DEV_LOGIN; an explicitly supplied compiled developer pair takes precedence and hides the developer-entry rows. Personal ScreenScraper account login remains a separate requirement. This request revisits developer provisioning now that pixelelated is a separate distro; no credential value is needed in tracking.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes for build-time selection, UI, account separation, failed-auth handling, and backup exclusion. ScreenScraper authorization for distributing a shared/fork developer identity is an external dependency, not something inferred from ROCKNIX packaging.

- [x] Record the owner-selected interim JELOS developer identity and separate replacement work into #586 (D-WORKFLOW-166). This records the project decision, not new provider authorization or completed provisioning.
- [ ] Implement and document the selected interim developer provisioning route and applicable artifact checks; reconcile current runtime-only comments and historical guard descriptions under D-WORKFLOW-166. Preserve unrelated private-credential protections; prove actual checks execute.
- [ ] Implement approved release provisioning without requiring ordinary players to enter developer credentials; keep their own account login distinct and preserve working runtime fallback as appropriate.
- [ ] Review English/French accounts/options/error flows at small/large sizes, update canonical IA/menu/flow references and source-bound frames, and verify clean/upgrade plus credential backup exclusions.

Current M7 work; related #64/#66/#528. Dedicated/replacement credentials are separate backlog #586. No embedding change or provider outreach is claimed by this tracker update.
## Historical initial read-only triage

Initial source check confirms runtime developer entry is intentional under D-QA-005/006. Existing compiled-pair precedence could support hiding those developer rows once an approved distribution identity is selected. No provider authorization for pixelelated reuse has been established here; no shared pair was embedded or copied. A dedicated pixelelated developer identity is the preferred evaluation path, with an interim shared identity considered only if its use is explicitly supported.

Evidence record: [owner-feedback triage](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/960b4d8c358b1e74b501ffdc329532be67cf7f6e/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-12-owner-feedback/README.md).

## Historical activation — October 12

Owner: “Let's work through 565, 566, and 567 now.” Moved into M7.P5 in that order. #569 read-only incident diagnosis is an immediate interruption; #564 and #493 remain the next foundation/build gates. Existing acceptance criteria and VM-first scope remain.

## Historical October 13 provider dependency check

The [official API documentation](https://www.screenscraper.fr/webapi2.php), checked October 13, directs application developers to its forum to obtain developer credentials. Developer identity and player account credentials are separate. Public visibility of a shared pair does not establish authorization for this fork.

At that checkpoint, owner clarification was pending on whether an approved pixelelated developer identity already existed; October 14 interim selection below supersedes that pending project choice. No forum contact, credential embedding or runtime fallback change occurred. The existing working route was preserved. Provider registration/replacement evaluation now belongs to #586; the interim choice no longer awaits clarification. [Dated dependency record](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/0ea6eaf74ad47503c05955d1c0bd4bd00bdfb816/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-13-es-trim-comparison/screenscraper-dependency.md).

Can this be done on the VM? Yes. A fresh no-NIC GENERIC_X64 VM20 allocation will exercise the complete selected-state root-policy suite plus four synthetic recipe selection cases (unset, empty, shared and explicit local override). The new suite also runs against the unchanged gate/recipe as deliberate failing controls. Source candidate supplies the selected shared developer pair; the gate only permits the exact NUL-delimited pair in ES ELF, not personal accounts, different pairs, embedded RA keys or seeded settings. Parser ELF fixtures are synthetic, not actual ES execution.

Owner `/workspace/tmp/pix566-vm-20261014a`, standard8GiB/4CPU640x480,15-minute lifecycle ceiling,180-second root suite limits/30-second recipe limits and256MiB output. Fresh retention/admission plus original watcher/launcher/guest receipts required. All disks/media retire after result export. No provider/device/account operation, ES pin change or image acceptance. Actual compiled/UI/frame/backup/payload checks remain due. Canonical proposed flow is in docs/es-menu-map.md.

Interim provisioning candidate19221f4762298b10e44a08f2c3e7371c7ddeb0d1 is implemented locally. A fresh offline VM passes127 selected-state root-policy cases (113 existing +14 new) and four recipe environment cases: unset, empty, explicit shared and explicit local override. The new controls fail against unchanged source as expected (gate2/recipe1); candidate outputs0. Only the exact NUL-delimited compiled shared identity is permitted; other developer/RA pairs and player/default settings remain refused. All original successful-run delivery channels0, actual host/QEMU owners exited, admission consumed and disks retired.

Original attempt01 remainsFAIL1 from a generated report's nested newline syntax error; failure cleanup also stopped before flushing its output, so no test pass is accepted from it. Fresh attempt02 syntax-checks shell and embedded Python and records successful output unmount before stop. Both temporary disk sets are retired (4,554,809,344 bytes). Compact local evidence is docs/qa-logs/2026-10-14-screenscraper-provisioning/; no provider or owner-device operation.

Actual rebuilt ES definition/URL selection, reviewed EN/FR small/large frames, backup and final clean/retained images remain open. Header-shaped ELF parser fixtures are not actual binary qualification. Canonical flow is updated with those frame obligations. #586 remains backlog. No pin promotion, push or RC designation.
